clauses.text:
75/-
Executive ether,
When transfers or promotions are properly applied for, and are other-
wise permissible, the Civil Service Commission is hereby authorized, in its
discretion, looking to the good of the public service only, to waive require-
ments for examination and to substitute for such examination so waived
such other tests of fitness and capacity as the Commission may decide.
I n each case where such waiver is made the reasons therefor shall be
stated at length by the Commnission and made matter of record in its
minutes.
THEODORE ROOSEVELT
THE WHIITE HOUSE,
November 22, 1907.
[7511

ACTOR_TEXT:EO:1266.text:
Executive Orber.
The Civil Service Commission is hereby authorized to except from
competitive examination, as contemplated by the civil-service act, Section
2, Clause Second, subject to the limitations prescribed by the Statute and
those now set forth in Rule II, certain positions arising, of unusual char-
acter, as to duties, and for which qualified persons are so rare, that, in the
judgment of the Commission, they cannot, in the interests of good civil
service administration, be filled through open competitive examination.
In every instance of the exercise of this power the same procedure shall
he followed as required in the Executive order of November 22, 1907.
WM H TAFT
THE WHITE HOUSE,
December I, 1.r.
[No. 1266.]
I
